chunks: And with this chain, from al-Hasan, from Sayf ibn 'Umaira, from Ibn [Abi] Bakr al-Hadrami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

One who has faith in Allah and the Last Day must not fail to recite 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad' after the obligatory prayer; for whoever recites it, Allah will gather for him the goodness of this world and the hereafter, and Allah will forgive him, his parents, and what he has begotten.

key_terms.خَيْرَ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ: The goodness of this world and the hereafter
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, the One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas after obligatory prayers?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith highlights the specific merit of reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas immediately after obligatory prayers, linking it to the comprehensive reward of worldly and hereafter goodness. It uniquely extends the spiritual benefit of forgiveness to the reciter's parents and offspring, reflecting the Shia emphasis on familial intercession and the purifying power of Tawhid. This practice underscores the belief that sincere monotheistic devotion serves as a means of securing divine mercy for one's lineage.
